recto: Total calcium vs ionized calcium, adult intervals
verso: Total: 8.6–10.2 mg/dL (2.15–2.55 mmol/L). Ionized: 1.16–1.31 mmol/L (4.65–5.25 mg/dL). Factor × {x:F_CA}

recto: Fasting plasma glucose adult reference interval
Hemoglobin A1c reference interval and SI unit
verso: 4.0–5.6 % (20–38 mmol/mol IFCC). NGSP master equation: % = {v:ngsp_pente} × mmol/mol + {v:ngsp_ordonnee}, so mmol/mol = (% − {v:ngsp_ordonnee}) ÷ {v:ngsp_pente}
BUN 8–20 mg/dL (urea 2.9–7.1 mmol/L). Creatinine: female 0.50–1.10, male 0.70–1.30 mg/dL (44–97 and 62–115 µmol/L)
Hb: female 12–16, male 14–18 g/dL (× {x:F_GDL} = g/L). Hct: female 37–47 %, male 42–50 % (0.37–0.47 and 0.42–0.50 L/L)

recto: PT, aPTT and INR without anticoagulant
verso: PT 11–13 s; aPTT 25–35 s (ABIM). INR 0.8–1.1 (MedlinePlus)

recto: INR target on warfarin and bleeding risk
verso: Set by the prescriber; it depends on the indication. {v:inr_caillot}–{v:inr_saignement} is common. Above {v:inr_saignement}: higher bleeding risk; below {v:inr_caillot}: clot risk (MedlinePlus). Report per protocol

recto: Why is BUN not the same number as urea?
verso: BUN is urea nitrogen; urea has 2 N atoms: BUN (mg/dL) × {x:F_BUN} = urea (mmol/L)

recto: Albumin, total bilirubin, ALT and AST (adult)
verso: Albumin 3.5–5.5 g/dL (35–55 g/L); total bilirubin 0.3–1.0 mg/dL (5–17 µmol/L); ALT and AST 10–40 U/L each
Total cholesterol desirable < 200 mg/dL; LDL optimal < 100 mg/dL; HDL is low if < 50 (female) or < 40 (male); triglycerides normal < 150 mg/dL
0.5–1.9 ng/mL (0.6–2.4 nmol/L): a general range (MedlinePlus); the right level may vary with the situation: follow the prescriber's target
